title: Rosemary and eucalyptus simmer pot
subtitle: A stovetop simmering blend for a clean, herbal house scent
excerpt: A stovetop simmer pot of fresh rosemary, eucalyptus leaves, lemon slices, and black peppercorns in water. Simmered on the hob on a low heat, it releases a clean, herbal scent throughout the kitchen and adjoining rooms. Simmer for 1-3 hours, topping up with water as needed. Ingredients for one pot.
sourceNotes: Stovetop simmer pot method: open-vessel evaporation of volatile compounds from whole botanicals in hot water. Rosemary (Rosmarinus officinalis): main volatile compounds, camphor, 1,8-cineole, alpha-pinene; herbal-clean scent. Eucalyptus (Eucalyptus globulus fresh leaves or dried): 1,8-cineole dominant; sharp, clean, medicinal note. Lemon (Citrus limon fresh slices): limonene volatilises rapidly from the peel in hot water. Black pepper (Piper nigrum cracked): piperine degrades on heating; primarily provides spice-floral volatiles (beta-caryophyllene). Simmer rather than boil: boiling too aggressively causes rapid evaporation, low simmer releases scent slowly and safely. Never leave unattended. Discard after use.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare the pot up to a day ahead and refrigerate. Bring to a simmer when ready. Discard after simmering; do not refrigerate used botanicals.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Use immediately once simmered; discard botanicals after use. Prepared-but-unheated contents can be refrigerated for up to 24 hours before simmering.

glossaryTerms.definition: A pot of water with botanical ingredients simmered on the hob to release volatile aromatic compounds as steam. A low-cost, chemical-free alternative to synthetic air fresheners or reed diffusers.

content.text: is fresh rosemary, eucalyptus leaves, lemon slices, and cracked black pepper simmered in water on the hob. The steam carries their volatile compounds into the room, a clean, herbal, mildly medicinal scent. Simmer on the lowest heat that keeps a gentle bubble; boiling hard evaporates the water too quickly and produces less scent. Never leave unattended. Ingredients for one pot; discard after use.

items.prepNote: in a small saucepan on the lowest heat; top up as needed
6-8 leaves; fresh or dried; fresh from a florist also works
approx. 1 tsp, cracked; adds a warm spicy note

content.text: Combine all ingredients in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Reduce to the lowest heat that maintains a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil. Leave the lid off.
Top up with water every 30-45 minutes. Never allow the pot to boil dry, keep checking the water level.
Remove from the heat after 1-3 hours. Discard the botanicals. Do not leave simmering overnight or in an empty room.
